exam_context.frequency: High: motion calculations and graphs appear in almost every paper

opener.display:
Picture a car pulling away from traffic lights. Every second it gains the same amount of speed.
After 4 seconds it is moving at 12 m/s.
opener.label: Before any equations

steps.say: No equations yet, just share it out. It gained 12 m/s evenly over 4 seconds.

steps.hint: 3 m/s gained each second, for 2 seconds.
steps.pre: So after 2 seconds it is moving at
steps.say: That steady 3 m/s every second has a name: acceleration.
That is all acceleration is: the speed added each second. As an equation, acceleration = change in speed ÷ time = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 m/s². The little ² just means 'per second, each second'.

bronze.display: A runner covers 400 m in 50 s. Calculate the average speed.
bronze.label: Together: your first one

steps.say: Speed tells you the distance covered each second. The equation: speed = distance ÷ time.

steps.done: That is the speed in m/s.
Back to the 400 m we started with. Correct.

steps.say: So the average speed is 8 m/s.

gold.display: A motorbike accelerates from rest at 4 m/s² over 18 m. Using v² = u² + 2as, find its final speed.
gold.label: Together: the gold move

steps.say: Two moves here: substitute into v² = u² + 2as, then square root at the end. Start from rest, so u = 0.

steps.done: That final root is the trap.
steps.hint: The square-root step, easy to miss.

steps.say: So the final speed is 12 m/s.

silver.display: A car travelling at 72 km/h brakes to rest in 5 s. Calculate the deceleration in m/s².
silver.label: Together: the silver move

steps.say: The speed is in km/h but the answer needs m/s². Convert the units first, the silver move.

steps.done: Now everything is in the right units.
Four metres per second squared of braking.
That is the 20 m/s it lost. Correct.
steps.hint: Deceleration × time gives the speed lost.

method_card.content:
Two equations and two graph types cover this lesson.

Speed: average speed (m/s) = distance (m) ÷ time (s).

Acceleration: a (m/s²) = change in speed (m/s) ÷ time (s). A negative value means deceleration.

Distance-time graph: gradient = speed; a horizontal line means stationary.

Velocity-time graph: gradient = acceleration; area under the line = distance.

Watch out: use the change in speed (not the final speed) for acceleration, and use ½ × base × height for a triangle's area.
steps: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time (m/s²). Change in speed = final − start
Distance-time graph: gradient = speed; a flat line means stationary
Velocity-time graph: gradient = acceleration; area under the line = distance
method_card.title: Speed, Acceleration and Motion Graphs

bronze.display: A cyclist travels 540 m in 60 s. Calculate their average speed in m/s.

guided_steps.say: Speed = distance ÷ time. The values are already in metres and seconds, so no converting.

guided_steps.pre: Substitute the numbers: speed = 540 ÷ __ (the time in s)

guided_steps.done: That returns the distance, so 9 m/s is right.
guided_steps.hint: Speed × time should return the distance.

misconceptions.message: That looks like time ÷ distance. Speed is distance ÷ time: 540 ÷ 60 = 9 m/s.

bronze.display: A car travels at 25 m/s for 40 s. Calculate the distance covered.

guided_steps.say: Distance = speed × time. Units are already m/s and s.

guided_steps.done: That returns the speed, so 1,000 m is right.
guided_steps.hint: Distance ÷ time should give the speed back.

misconceptions.message: Distance = speed × time, so multiply: 25 × 40 = 1,000 m. Dividing (40 ÷ 25 = 1.6) uses the equation upside down.

bronze.display: A car accelerates from 0 m/s to 30 m/s in 6 s. Calculate its acceleration.

guided_steps.say: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time. It starts from rest, so the change is just 30 m/s.

guided_steps.hint: Change in speed divided by time.

guided_steps.done: That returns the speed gained, so 5 m/s² is right.
guided_steps.hint: Acceleration × time gives the change in speed.

misconceptions.message: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time = 30 ÷ 6 = 5 m/s². Dividing time by speed (6 ÷ 30) gives 0.2, which is upside down.

bronze.display: A ball decelerates from 24 m/s to 0 in 4 s. What is the magnitude of its acceleration in m/s²?
bronze.equation_hint: a = change in speed ÷ time. Change = 24 − 0 = 24 m/s.

guided_steps.say: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time. The ball slows to rest, so the change is 24 m/s.

guided_steps.hint: Change in speed divided by time.

guided_steps.done: That returns the speed lost, so the magnitude is 6 m/s².
guided_steps.hint: Size of acceleration × time gives the change.

guided_steps.say: The magnitude of the acceleration is 6 m/s².

misconceptions.message: The change is 24 − 0 = 24 m/s over 4 s, so a = 6 m/s². The question asks for magnitude, so the answer is positive 6, not −6.

bronze.display: A stone is dropped and falls for 3 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², calculate its final speed.
bronze.equation_hint: Final speed = acceleration × time (starting from rest)

guided_steps.say: Dropped from rest, so final speed = acceleration × time, with g = 10 m/s².

guided_steps.done: That returns g, so 30 m/s is right.
guided_steps.hint: Speed ÷ time should give g back.

misconceptions.message: This asks for the speed, not the distance. Speed = g × t = 10 × 3 = 30 m/s. (½ × 10 × 3² = 45 m would be the distance fallen.)

bronze.equation_hint: Divide km/h by 3.6 to get m/s

guided_steps.say: To change km/h into m/s, divide by 3.6.

guided_steps.pre: Write the speed to convert: __ km/h

guided_steps.done: That returns 90 km/h, so 25 m/s is right.

misconceptions.message: To go from km/h to m/s, divide by 3.6: 90 ÷ 3.6 = 25 m/s. Multiplying by 3.6 (324) goes the wrong way.

problem_bank.bronze_description: One equation, values already in m and s: substitute and go.

gold.display: A car brakes from 20 m/s and stops in 50 m. Using v² − u² = 2as (where u = 20, v = 0, s = 50), calculate the deceleration.

guided_steps.say: Rearrange v² − u² = 2as to find a: a = (v² − u²) ÷ (2s). Here u = 20, v = 0, s = 50.

guided_steps.hint: This is negative because it slows down.

guided_steps.done: 4 m/s², matching a car braking hard.
guided_steps.hint: Drop the minus sign for the size.
guided_steps.say: The question asks for the size of the deceleration.

misconceptions.message: The calculation gives −4 m/s² (the car is slowing). The question wants the size, so the deceleration is 4 m/s².

gold.display: A stone is dropped from a 45 m cliff (g = 10 m/s²). Using v² = u² + 2as, calculate the speed when it hits the ground.
gold.equation_hint: v² = u² + 2as, then take the square root for v

guided_steps.say: Use v² = u² + 2as. Dropped from rest so u = 0, a = 10, s = 45.

guided_steps.hint: Add u², which is zero here.

guided_steps.say: Take the square root, the step people forget:
The stone hits the ground at 30 m/s.

misconceptions.message: v² = 900, so take the square root: v = √900 = 30 m/s. Stopping at 900 forgets the square root.
v² = 2as = 2 × 10 × 45 = 900. Leaving out the 2 gives 450 and v ≈ 21.2 m/s, which is wrong.

gold.display: A velocity-time graph shows a car: 0 to 25 m/s in 5 s, constant speed 25 m/s for 10 s, then decelerates to rest in 5 s. Calculate the total distance.
gold.equation_hint: Distance = area under the line (triangles use ½ × base × height)

guided_steps.say: Distance = total area. Split into triangle, rectangle, triangle.

guided_steps.done: Plus the 250 rectangle gives 375 m, so it is right.

misconceptions.message: The two sloped sections are triangles: ½ × 5 × 25 = 62.5 m each. With the middle rectangle 10 × 25 = 250 m, the total is 375 m. Forgetting the ½ gives 500.

problem_bank.gold_description: Chain two steps: v² = u² + 2as with a square root, or a multi-part graph area.

silver.display: A car accelerates from 5 m/s to 25 m/s in 8 s. Calculate the acceleration.

guided_steps.say: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time. This one does NOT start from rest, so find the change first.

guided_steps.done: Start speed plus the gain returns 25 m/s, so 2.5 m/s² is right.

misconceptions.message: Use the CHANGE in speed, not the final speed: 25 − 5 = 20 m/s, so a = 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5 m/s². Using 25 gives 3.125.

silver.display: A velocity-time graph shows acceleration from 0 to 20 m/s over 10 s. Calculate the distance covered (area under the line).
silver.equation_hint: Area of triangle = ½ × base × height

guided_steps.say: Distance = area under a velocity-time line. This section is a triangle.

guided_steps.done: Same 100 m, so it is right.
guided_steps.say: Check using average speed: average = ½ × 20 = 10 m/s, over 10 s:

misconceptions.message: The shape is a triangle, so area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 20 = 100 m. Using base × height (200) forgets the ½.

silver.display: After the acceleration phase above, the car travels at constant 20 m/s for 20 s. Calculate the distance covered in this section.

guided_steps.say: Constant speed, so the graph section is a rectangle. Distance = area = base × height.

guided_steps.done: That returns the speed, so 400 m is right.
guided_steps.hint: Distance ÷ time gives the speed back.

guided_steps.say: The distance in this section is 400 m.

misconceptions.message: This section is a rectangle (constant speed), so area = base × height = 20 × 20 = 400 m. No ½ here; that is only for triangles.

silver.display: A car decelerates from 30 m/s to rest in 5 s. Calculate the deceleration.
silver.equation_hint: a = change in speed ÷ time. Change = 30 − 0 = 30 m/s.

guided_steps.say: Deceleration = change in speed ÷ time. It slows to rest, so the change is 30 m/s.

guided_steps.done: That returns the speed lost, so 6 m/s² is right.

misconceptions.message: Deceleration = change ÷ time = 30 ÷ 5 = 6 m/s². Dividing time by change (5 ÷ 30 = 0.17) is upside down.

silver.display: A train accelerates from rest to 30 m/s in 10 s, travels at constant speed for 20 s, then decelerates to rest in 5 s. Calculate the total distance in metres.
silver.equation_hint: Add three area sections: triangle + rectangle + triangle

guided_steps.say: Split the graph into three areas: a triangle, a rectangle, and a triangle. Find each, then add.

guided_steps.done: That returns the 20 s of steady speed, so 825 m stands.
guided_steps.hint: Rectangle distance ÷ speed gives its time.

misconceptions.message: The sloped sections are triangles, so halve them: ½ × 10 × 30 = 150 and ½ × 5 × 30 = 75. With the 600 rectangle, total = 825 m. Forgetting the halves gives 1050.

problem_bank.silver_description: Convert the units or find the change in speed first, or read a distance off a graph.

example.question: A runner covers 300 m in 60 s. Find the average speed.

steps: Pick the equation the words point to: speed = distance ÷ time, or acceleration = change in speed ÷ time.
The values are already in the right units (metres and seconds), so substitute them straight in.
Divide, then write the answer with its unit, m/s or m/s².
bronze.title: Bronze: one equation, straight in

example.question: A car accelerates from rest at 3 m/s² over 24 m. Find its final speed (v² = u² + 2as).

steps: These need more than one move: a graph split into several areas, or the equation v² = u² + 2as (check whether your board gives you this one).
With v² = u² + 2as, substitute the numbers, then take the square root at the end to find v. Missing that root is the classic slip.
For a multi-part graph, work out each section's area and add them up.
gold.title: Gold: chain two steps

example.question: A car speeds up from 6 m/s to 24 m/s in 9 s. Find the acceleration.

steps: One thing is not ready yet: either convert the units (km/h ÷ 3.6 = m/s) or find the change in speed (final − start) before dividing.
Do that single set-up step first, and it becomes a bronze question.
For a velocity-time graph, distance = area under the line: triangle = ½ × base × height, rectangle = base × height.
silver.title: Silver: convert or rearrange first

worked_examples.question: A cyclist travels 540 m in 60 s. Calculate their average speed.
A car accelerates from 5 m/s to 25 m/s in 8 s. Calculate the acceleration.
A train accelerates from rest to 30 m/s in 10 s, then travels at 30 m/s for 20 s. Calculate the total distance travelled.
